long_biography.plain_text:
A decade of permitting preceded work on a shallow mudflat below Seattle's Magnolia neighbourhood. Construction began in 1989, and the facility opened two years later. It had more than 1,200 slips, ten miles of dock space and room for visiting boats of many sizes. The site grew into a full-service waterfront community offering repairs, fuel, retail and dining close to downtown.

Kaiser represented the local ownership group through the property's next chapter. When that partnership transferred the business to Southern Marinas, he described the decision as the right time to place operations with a specialist team. The handoff brought the original owners' long stewardship to an end while leaving their infrastructure and boating community under new management.
